nodes.name: Open **Quick start** in the app and choose the workspace…
nodes.text: Open **Quick start** in the app and choose the workspace you want the connection to use. It shows the installation and login steps for your harness with your workspace ID filled in. The public quick start in the developer docs shows the same steps with placeholders.

nodes.name: The client is one Node.js file, `nulldull.mjs`, that…
nodes.text: The client is one Node.js file, `nulldull.mjs`, that provides both the CLI and a local MCP server. It needs Node.js 22 or newer. Register one MCP server named `nulldull` in your harness and start a new session.

nodes.name: `login` starts a browser-approved device login. Check that…
nodes.text: `login` starts a browser-approved device login. Check that the code in the browser matches the one in your terminal, confirm the workspace, choose what the agent may do in Memory—**read**, **propose** or **edit**—and approve. The client stores its credential in your private configuration directory, outside your repositories, and never prints it.

nodes.name: New connections last six calendar months, including after…
nodes.text: New connections last six calendar months, including after you sign out of the browser. Every request still checks your membership, verified identity, early access and current permissions.

nodes.name: Since client 0.18.0, each workspace keeps its own login.…
nodes.text: Since client 0.18.0, each workspace keeps its own login. `login` binds the directory it runs in to the approved workspace, and subdirectories inherit the nearest binding. Projects that use different workspaces stay signed in at the same time.

nodes.name: - `workspaces` lists the workspaces you are signed in to…
nodes.text:
- `workspaces` lists the workspaces you are signed in to and the one this directory uses.
- `use WORKSPACE_ID` points a directory at a workspace you are already signed in to, without a browser login. `use --clear` removes the binding.
- `logout` signs out of the selected workspace only.

nodes.name: A command uses `--workspace`, then the…
nodes.text: A command uses `--workspace`, then the `NULLDULL_WORKSPACE` environment variable, then the nearest bound directory, then your default login. Before writing, importing or exporting, run `status` to confirm the origin and workspace.

nodes.name: Grant only what the task needs.
nodes.text: ## Grant only what the task needs.

nodes.name: Memory read, propose and edit modes control what the agent…
nodes.text: Memory read, propose and edit modes control what the agent may do within your current access. Grid, Secrets, Locale and Tasks each have a separate capability, off by default. Owners and admins can also allow the agent to create products and projects. A Memory grant never opens another product.

nodes.name: An agent must read the current version before replacing…
nodes.text: An agent must read the current version before replacing existing content. When a change needs review, a submitted proposal is not yet a committed edit. No connection can create workspaces, administer access, approve changes or manage billing.

nodes.name: Open **Settings → Your agent connections** to inspect…
nodes.text: Open **Settings → Your agent connections** to inspect active connections. **Edit permissions** changes a connection’s capabilities; the agent uses the new permissions on its next request. You can revoke a connection at any time. A connection can never exceed your current membership and resource access.

nodes.name: The client checks for updates but never installs one on…
nodes.text: The client checks for updates but never installs one on its own. Approve the exact version and checksum it reports, then restart or reconnect the MCP server so the running session uses the new client.
